title: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act
shortDesc: The Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025 promotes e-sports and online social games while completely prohibiting online money games, their advertisement, and related fund transfers. It establishes an Authority to classify and register online games, and prescribes penalties including up to 3 years' imprisonment or a Rs.1 crore fine.

provisions.title: Short title, extent and commencement
provisions.text: May be called the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025; extends to the whole of India and also applies to an online money gaming service offered within India or operated from outside India; comes into force on a date notified by the Central Government.

provisions.title: Definitions
provisions.text: Defines the key terms, including 'advertisement' (per the Consumer Protection Act, 2019), 'Authority' (s.8), 'e-sport' (2(1)(c)), 'online game' (f), 'online money game' (g), 'online money gaming service' (h), 'online social game' (i), 'other stakes' (j), 'person' (k) and 'user' (m). Words not defined here take their meaning from the Information Technology Act, 2000.

title: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act
shortDesc: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 governs the processing of digital personal data in India, balancing individuals' privacy rights with lawful processing needs. It sets consent and notice requirements, imposes obligations on Data Fiduciaries, grants Data Principals rights of access, correction and erasure, and establishes the Data Protection Board, with penalties up to Rs.250 crore for breaches.

provisions.title: Short title and commencement
provisions.text: This Act may be called the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and comes into force on such date(s) as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint.

provisions.title: Definitions
provisions.text: Defines the key terms used in the Act, including 'personal data', 'Data Principal', 'Data Fiduciary', 'Data Processor' (clause (k)), 'consent', 'Consent Manager', 'child', 'personal data breach' and the 'Board'.
rules: DPDP-DPR-POB-1 (Processor): Enter into a valid contract with the Data Fiduciary before any processing. Penalty: Up to Rs.250 crore — Security failure attributable to the processor (liability flows to the Data Fiduciary under Sec 8(5); recoverable via the processing contract) (Schedule, entry 1 (Sec 8(5)))

DPDP-DPR-POB-2 (Processor): Process personal data only on the documented instructions and specified purpose of the Data Fiduciary. Penalty: Up to Rs.250 crore — Security failure attributable to the processor (liability flows to the Data Fiduciary under Sec 8(5); recoverable via the processing contract) (Schedule, entry 1 (Sec 8(5)))

DPDP-DPR-POB-3 (Processor): Apply reasonable technical and organizational security safeguards. Penalty: Up to Rs.250 crore — Security failure attributable to the processor (liability flows to the Data Fiduciary under Sec 8(5); recoverable via the processing contract) (Schedule, entry 1 (Sec 8(5)))

DPDP-DPR-POB-4 (Processor): Assist the Data Fiduciary in responding to Data Principal access/correction/erasure requests. Penalty: Up to Rs.250 crore — Security failure attributable to the processor (liability flows to the Data Fiduciary under Sec 8(5); recoverable via the processing contract) (Schedule, entry 1 (Sec 8(5)))

DPDP-DPR-POB-5 (Processor): Detect and notify the Data Fiduciary of any personal data breach without delay. Penalty: Up to Rs.250 crore — Security failure attributable to the processor (liability flows to the Data Fiduciary under Sec 8(5); recoverable via the processing contract) (Schedule, entry 1 (Sec 8(5)))

DPDP-DPR-POB-6 (Processor): Erase or return personal data on instruction or when the purpose is served. Penalty: Up to Rs.250 crore — Security failure attributable to the processor (liability flows to the Data Fiduciary under Sec 8(5); recoverable via the processing contract) (Schedule, entry 1 (Sec 8(5)))

DPDP-DPR-POB-7 (Processor): Maintain processing records and enable the Data Fiduciary’s audits and inspections. Penalty: Up to Rs.250 crore — Security failure attributable to the processor (liability flows to the Data Fiduciary under Sec 8(5); recoverable via the processing contract) (Schedule, entry 1 (Sec 8(5)))

provisions.title: Application of Act
provisions.text: Applies to the processing of digital personal data within India, and to processing outside India where it is in connection with offering goods or services to Data Principals in India. Excludes personal/domestic processing and personal data made publicly available by the Data Principal or under a legal obligation.

provisions.title: Grounds for processing personal data
provisions.text: A person may process the personal data of a Data Principal only for a lawful purpose for which the Data Principal has given consent, or for certain legitimate uses.

provisions.title: Duties of Data Principal
provisions.text: A Data Principal must comply with the law, not impersonate another, not suppress material information, not register a false or frivolous grievance/complaint, and furnish only authentic information.
rules: Furnish authentic information; do not file false or frivolous complaints.

provisions.title: Processing of personal data outside India
provisions.text: The Central Government may, by notification, restrict the transfer of personal data by a Data Fiduciary to any country or territory outside India.
rules: Comply with any restriction notified on cross-border transfer.

provisions.title: Exemptions
provisions.text: Provides exemptions from specified provisions - e.g. for enforcement of legal rights, judicial/regulatory functions, prevention/investigation of offences, and processing by notified instrumentalities of the State in the interests of sovereignty, security, public order, etc.

provisions.title: Establishment of Board
provisions.text: The Central Government shall establish the Data Protection Board of India.

provisions.title: Composition and qualifications for appointment of Chairperson and Members
provisions.text: Provides for the composition of the Board and the qualifications for appointment of its Chairperson and Members.

provisions.title: Salary, allowances payable to and term of office

provisions.title: Disqualifications for appointment and continuation as Chairperson and Members of Board
provisions.text: Sets out the disqualifications for appointment and for continuation as Chairperson or Member.

provisions.title: Resignation by Members and filling of vacancy

provisions.title: Proceedings of Board

provisions.title: Officers and employees of Board

provisions.title: Members and officers to be public servants
provisions.text: Members and officers of the Board are deemed public servants.

provisions.title: Powers of Chairperson
provisions.text: Provides for the powers of the Chairperson over the general superintendence and management of the Board.

provisions.text: The Board may accept a voluntary undertaking from any person in respect of any matter related to compliance; acceptance bars further proceedings on that matter, and breach of the undertaking is punishable as a breach of the Act.

provisions.title: Crediting sums realised by way of penalties to Consolidated Fund of India

provisions.title: Protection of action taken in good faith

provisions.title: Power to call for information

provisions.title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
provisions.text: Empowers the Central Government to issue directions, including to block information in the interest of the general public on a reference from the Board.

provisions.title: Consistency with other laws
provisions.text: The Act has effect in addition to and not in derogation of other laws; in case of conflict on data protection, this Act generally prevails.

provisions.title: Bar of jurisdiction
provisions.text: No civil court has jurisdiction over any matter which the Board or the Appellate Tribunal is empowered to determine.

provisions.title: Power to make rules

title: Aadhaar Act
shortDesc: The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016 establishes the UIDAI and provides for targeted delivery of subsidies, benefits and services through Aadhaar. It governs enrolment, authentication and offline verification, restricts sharing of identity information, and prescribes civil penalties and offences.

provisions.title: Short title, extent and commencement
provisions.text: May be called the Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016; extends to the whole of India (subject to J&K reorganisation) and comes into force on notified dates.

provisions.title: Definitions
provisions.text: Defines the key terms, including 'Aadhaar number', 'authentication', 'biometric information', 'core biometric information', 'demographic information', 'identity information', 'requesting entity', 'offline verification-seeking entity', 'Central Identities Data Repository' and 'resident'.

provisions.title: Aadhaar number
provisions.text: Every resident is entitled to obtain an Aadhaar number by submitting demographic and biometric information during enrolment; the enrolling agency must inform the resident of the manner of use and sharing of information (3(2)).
rules: (Enrolling agency) At enrolment, inform the resident of how the information will be used and shared (s.3(2)).

provisions.title: Aadhaar number of children
provisions.text: Provides for enrolment and the Aadhaar number of children, with consent of the parent/guardian and an option to cancel on attaining 18.

provisions.title: Properties of Aadhaar number
provisions.text: An Aadhaar number is unique, may be used/accepted as proof of identity subject to authentication or offline verification; a virtual/alternative number may be used to conceal the actual Aadhaar number.

provisions.title: Special measures for issuance of Aadhaar number to certain category of persons
provisions.text: The Authority shall take special measures to issue Aadhaar numbers to women, children, senior citizens, persons with disability, unskilled/migrant workers and other disadvantaged groups.

provisions.title: Update of certain information
provisions.text: The Authority may require Aadhaar number holders to update their demographic/biometric information to maintain accuracy of the CIDR.
rules: (Aadhaar number holder) Update demographic/biometric information as required.

provisions.title: Proof of Aadhaar number necessary for receipt of certain subsidies, benefits and services
provisions.text: The Central/State Government may require Aadhaar authentication (or proof of possession) as a condition for receipt of a subsidy, benefit or service funded from the Consolidated Fund; alternate means must be provided where authentication fails.
rules: Provide an alternate means of identification where Aadhaar authentication is not possible.

provisions.title: Authentication of Aadhaar number
provisions.text: The Authority shall perform authentication on a request by a requesting entity; the requesting entity must obtain consent of the individual (8(2)), inform them of the nature of information shared and alternatives (8(3)), and use identity information only for the submitted purpose.
rules: (Requesting entity) Obtain the individual's informed consent before authentication (s.8(2)); inform them of the use and alternatives (s.8(3)); use identity information only for the stated purpose.

AAD-RE-01 (RequestingEntity): Obtain informed consent before authentication. Breach: Failure to obtain the individual's informed consent before authentication / offline verification. Penalty: Unauthorised use of identity information in contravention of s.8(2)/s.8A(2) -> s.40 (imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine up to Rs.10,000 / Rs.1 lakh for a company, or both); plus civil penalty up to Rs.1 crore (s.33A, adjudicated u/s 33B).

AAD-RE-02 (RequestingEntity): Use identity information only for the stated purpose. Breach: Using identity information for a purpose other than the one disclosed to the individual. Penalty: Unauthorised use by a requesting entity -> s.40 (up to 3 years / fine); unauthorised disclosure -> s.37; plus civil penalty up to Rs.1 crore (s.33A).

provisions.title: Offline verification of Aadhaar number
provisions.text: Provides for offline verification of an Aadhaar number by an offline verification-seeking entity, with the consent of the individual and without seeking core biometric information.
rules: (Offline verification-seeking entity) Obtain consent; do not seek core biometric information; use information only for the stated purpose (s.8A(2)-(3)).

provisions.title: Aadhaar number not evidence of citizenship or domicile, etc.
provisions.text: An Aadhaar number or authentication is not, by itself, proof of citizenship or domicile.

provisions.title: Central Identities Data Repository
provisions.text: The Authority may establish and maintain one or more Central Identities Data Repositories (CIDR).

provisions.title: Establishment of Authority
provisions.text: Establishes the Unique Identification Authority of India as a statutory body.

provisions.title: Composition of Authority
provisions.text: Provides for the composition of the Authority (Chairperson and Members).

provisions.title: Qualifications for appointment of Chairperson and Members of Authority
provisions.text: Sets the qualifications for appointment of the Chairperson and Members.

provisions.title: Term of office and other conditions of service of Chairperson and Members
provisions.text: Provides for the term and conditions of service of the Chairperson and Members.

provisions.title: Removal of Chairperson and Members
provisions.text: Provides for the removal of the Chairperson and Members.

provisions.title: Restrictions on Chairperson or Members on employment after cessation of office
provisions.text: Restricts post-office employment of the Chairperson/Members.

provisions.title: Functions of Chairperson
provisions.text: Provides for the functions of the Chairperson.

provisions.title: Chief executive officer
provisions.text: Provides for the Chief Executive Officer of the Authority.

provisions.title: Meetings of Authority
provisions.text: Provides for the meetings and procedure of the Authority.

provisions.title: Vacancies, etc., not to invalidate proceedings of Authority
provisions.text: Vacancies or defects do not invalidate the Authority's proceedings.

provisions.title: Officers and other employees of Authority
provisions.text: Provides for the officers and employees of the Authority.

provisions.title: Transfer of assets, liabilities of Authority
provisions.text: Provides for transfer of assets and liabilities to the Authority.

provisions.title: Powers and functions of Authority
provisions.text: Sets out the powers and functions of the Authority, including enrolment, authentication, maintaining the CIDR, and specifying processes by regulation.
rules: (Authority) Perform its statutory functions and maintain the security of the CIDR.

provisions.title: Power of Authority to issue directions
provisions.text: The Authority may issue directions to any entity in the Aadhaar ecosystem for the discharge of its functions; non-compliance attracts civil penalty under s.33A.
rules: (Entities in the Aadhaar ecosystem) Comply with directions issued by the Authority (s.23A).

provisions.title: Grants by Central Government
provisions.text: Provides for grants by the Central Government to the Authority.

provisions.title: Fund
provisions.text: Provides for the constitution of the Authority's Fund.

provisions.title: Accounts and audit
provisions.text: Provides for the accounts of the Authority and their audit by the CAG.

provisions.title: Returns and annual report, etc.
provisions.text: Provides for returns and the annual report of the Authority.

provisions.title: Security and confidentiality of information
provisions.text: The Authority shall ensure the security and confidentiality of identity information and authentication records, take measures to protect them, and prevent unauthorised access; it must not reveal identity information except as permitted.
rules: (Authority / entities) Ensure the security and confidentiality of identity information; protect it against unauthorised access.

AAD-RE-03 (RequestingEntity): Secure identity information held by the entity. Breach: Failure to implement security measures to protect identity information from unauthorised access. Penalty: Unauthorised access to the CIDR -> s.38 (imprisonment up to 10 years and fine not less than Rs.10 lakh); plus civil penalty up to Rs.1 crore (s.33A); residual general penalty s.42.

provisions.title: Restriction on sharing information
provisions.text: Core biometric information collected must not be shared, and identity information may be shared only in accordance with the Act and regulations; identity information may be used only for the purposes specified to the individual (29(3)).
rules: (All entities) Do not share core biometric information; use identity information only for the purpose disclosed to the individual (s.29(3)).

AAD-RE-02 (RequestingEntity): Use identity information only for the stated purpose. Breach: Using identity information for a purpose other than the one disclosed to the individual. Penalty: Unauthorised use by a requesting entity -> s.40 (up to 3 years / fine); unauthorised disclosure -> s.37; plus civil penalty up to Rs.1 crore (s.33A).

AAD-RE-03 (RequestingEntity): Secure identity information held by the entity. Breach: Failure to implement security measures to protect identity information from unauthorised access. Penalty: Unauthorised access to the CIDR -> s.38 (imprisonment up to 10 years and fine not less than Rs.10 lakh); plus civil penalty up to Rs.1 crore (s.33A); residual general penalty s.42.

AAD-RE-05 (RequestingEntity): Do not collect, use or store core biometric information. Breach: Collecting, using, storing or sharing core biometric information. Penalty: Sharing/using core biometric information in contravention of s.29 -> s.38 (up to 10 years and fine not less than Rs.10 lakh) / s.37 (disclosure); plus civil penalty up to Rs.1 crore (s.33A).

AAD-RE-06 (RequestingEntity): Report and remediate unauthorised access. Breach: Failure to report and remediate an unauthorised access to, or breach of, identity information. Penalty: Unauthorised access -> s.38 (up to 10 years and fine not less than Rs.10 lakh); tampering with CIDR data -> s.39 (up to 10 years); plus civil penalty up to Rs.1 crore (s.33A).

provisions.title: Biometric information deemed to be sensitive personal information
provisions.text: Biometric information is deemed an 'electronic record' and 'sensitive personal data or information'; the Information Technology Act, 2000 applies in addition to this Act.
rules: Treat biometric information as sensitive personal data and apply IT Act, 2000 safeguards.

AAD-RE-03 (RequestingEntity): Secure identity information held by the entity. Breach: Failure to implement security measures to protect identity information from unauthorised access. Penalty: Unauthorised access to the CIDR -> s.38 (imprisonment up to 10 years and fine not less than Rs.10 lakh); plus civil penalty up to Rs.1 crore (s.33A); residual general penalty s.42.

AAD-RE-05 (RequestingEntity): Do not collect, use or store core biometric information. Breach: Collecting, using, storing or sharing core biometric information. Penalty: Sharing/using core biometric information in contravention of s.29 -> s.38 (up to 10 years and fine not less than Rs.10 lakh) / s.37 (disclosure); plus civil penalty up to Rs.1 crore (s.33A).

provisions.title: Alteration of demographic information or biometric information
provisions.text: An Aadhaar number holder may request alteration of incorrect/changed demographic or biometric information; no CIDR information may be altered except as provided.
rules: (Aadhaar number holder) Request correction of incorrect information.

provisions.title: Access to own information and records of requests for authentication
provisions.text: The Authority shall maintain authentication records for the prescribed period and allow an Aadhaar number holder to access them; it shall not collect or keep the purpose of authentication.
rules: (Authority / requesting entities) Maintain authentication records for the prescribed period; provide access to the individual.

AAD-RE-04 (RequestingEntity): Maintain authentication records for the prescribed period. Breach: Failure to maintain authentication records for the prescribed period. Penalty: Civil penalty up to Rs.1 crore per contravention plus up to Rs.10 lakh/day continuing (s.33A, adjudicated u/s 33B); residual general penalty s.42.

provisions.title: Disclosure of information in certain cases
provisions.text: Identity information/authentication records may be disclosed only pursuant to an order of a court not inferior to a High Court Judge, or on a direction (reviewed by an Oversight Committee) in the interest of national security; core biometric information shall not be disclosed.

provisions.title: Penalty for failure to comply with provisions of this Act, rules, regulations and directions
provisions.text: An entity in the Aadhaar ecosystem that fails to comply with the Act, rules, regulations or directions (s.23A), or fails to furnish required information, is liable to a civil penalty up to Rs.1 crore per contravention, plus up to Rs.10 lakh per day for continuing failure.
rules: Comply with the Act, rules, regulations and the Authority's directions; furnish information when required.

provisions.title: Power to adjudicate
provisions.text: The Authority appoints an Adjudicating Officer (not below Joint Secretary) to hold an inquiry and impose the civil penalty under s.33A, after an opportunity of hearing.

provisions.title: Appeals to Appellate Tribunal
provisions.text: An appeal against an order of the Adjudicating Officer lies to the Appellate Tribunal.

provisions.title: Procedure and powers of the Appellate Tribunal
provisions.text: Provides for the procedure and powers of the Appellate Tribunal.

provisions.title: Appeal to Supreme Court of India
provisions.text: An appeal against an order of the Appellate Tribunal lies to the Supreme Court.

provisions.title: Civil court not to have jurisdiction
provisions.text: No civil court has jurisdiction over matters that the Adjudicating Officer or the Appellate Tribunal is empowered to determine.

provisions.title: Penalty for impersonation at time of enrolment
provisions.text: Impersonating another (by false demographic/biometric information) at enrolment is an offence.

provisions.title: Penalty for impersonation of Aadhaar number holder by changing demographic information or biometric information
provisions.text: Changing an Aadhaar number holder's demographic/biometric information with intent to harm or appropriate identity is an offence.

provisions.title: Penalty for impersonation
provisions.text: Pretending to be authorised to collect identity information, without authorisation, is an offence.

provisions.title: Penalty for disclosing identity information
provisions.text: Intentionally disclosing/transmitting identity information to an unauthorised person, or in contravention of an agreement, is an offence.
rules: Do not disclose identity information to any unauthorised person or in breach of the applicable agreement.

provisions.title: Penalty for unauthorised access to the Central Identities Data Repository
provisions.text: Unauthorised access, downloading, damage, disruption, or introducing a virus into the CIDR is an offence (enhanced punishment).
rules: Do not access or interfere with the CIDR without authorisation; report and remediate any unauthorised access.

AAD-RE-06 (RequestingEntity): Report and remediate unauthorised access. Breach: Failure to report and remediate an unauthorised access to, or breach of, identity information. Penalty: Unauthorised access -> s.38 (up to 10 years and fine not less than Rs.10 lakh); tampering with CIDR data -> s.39 (up to 10 years); plus civil penalty up to Rs.1 crore (s.33A).

provisions.title: Penalty for tampering with data in Central Identities Data Repository
provisions.text: Using or tampering with data in the CIDR to modify or discover information is an offence.
rules: Do not tamper with data in the CIDR.

AAD-RE-06 (RequestingEntity): Report and remediate unauthorised access. Breach: Failure to report and remediate an unauthorised access to, or breach of, identity information. Penalty: Unauthorised access -> s.38 (up to 10 years and fine not less than Rs.10 lakh); tampering with CIDR data -> s.39 (up to 10 years); plus civil penalty up to Rs.1 crore (s.33A).

provisions.title: Penalty for unauthorised use by requesting entity or offline verification-seeking entity
provisions.text: A requesting entity or offline verification-seeking entity that uses identity information in contravention of s.8(2)/s.8A(2) commits an offence.
rules: (Requesting / offline verification-seeking entity) Use identity information only as permitted by s.8(2)/s.8A(2).

provisions.title: Penalty for non-compliance with intimation requirements
provisions.text: An enrolling agency or requesting entity that fails to comply with the intimation requirements of s.3(2) or s.8(3) commits an offence.
rules: (Enrolling agency / requesting entity) Comply with the intimation duties in s.3(2)/s.8(3).

provisions.title: General penalty
provisions.text: Any contravention of the Act, rules or regulations for which no specific penalty is provided is punishable under this general penalty.

provisions.title: Offences by companies
provisions.text: Where an offence is committed by a company, the person in charge and responsible, and the company, are liable; officers liable where there is consent/connivance/neglect.
rules: (Company officers) Exercise due diligence to prevent commission of an offence.

provisions.title: Act to apply for offence or contravention committed outside India
provisions.text: The Act applies to offences/contraventions committed outside India involving a computer/system located in India.

provisions.title: Power to investigate offences
provisions.text: Provides for the investigation of offences by a police officer not below the rank of Inspector.

provisions.title: Penalties not to interfere with other punishments
provisions.text: Penalties under this Act are without prejudice to punishment under any other law.

provisions.title: Cognizance of offences
provisions.text: A court shall take cognizance of an offence only on a complaint made by the Authority or an officer/person authorised by it; only a court not inferior to a Court of Sessions may try such offences.

provisions.title: Power of Central Government to supersede Authority
provisions.text: The Central Government may, in specified circumstances, supersede the Authority.

provisions.title: Members, officers, etc., to be public servants
provisions.text: Members, officers and employees of the Authority are deemed public servants.

provisions.title: Power of Central Government to issue directions
provisions.text: The Central Government may issue directions to the Authority on policy matters.

provisions.title: Exemption from tax on income
provisions.text: Exempts the income of the Authority from tax.

provisions.title: Delegation
provisions.text: The Authority may delegate its powers and functions.

provisions.title: Protection of action taken in good faith
provisions.text: No suit or proceeding lies against the Government/Authority/officers for anything done in good faith.

provisions.title: Power of Central Government to make rules
provisions.text: The Central Government may make rules to carry out the provisions of the Act (the UIDAI Rules are made under this section).
rules: Comply with the rules made under s.53.

provisions.title: Power of Authority to make regulations
provisions.text: The Authority may make regulations (e.g. the Aadhaar Authentication and Offline Verification, Sharing of Information, Data Security, and Enrolment and Update Regulations) consistent with the Act.
rules: Comply with the regulations made under s.54.

provisions.title: Laying of rules and regulations before Parliament
provisions.text: Rules and regulations must be laid before each House of Parliament.

provisions.title: Application of other laws not barred
provisions.text: The Act's provisions are in addition to, and not in derogation of, other laws.

provisions.title: [Omitted.]
provisions.text: Section 57 (which permitted use of Aadhaar by the State or any body corporate/person under any law or contract) was struck down by the Supreme Court in K.S. Puttaswamy (2018) and stands omitted.

provisions.title: Power to remove difficulties
provisions.text: The Central Government may issue orders to remove difficulties within a limited period.

provisions.title: Savings
provisions.text: Validates actions taken under the earlier executive notifications relating to the UIDAI prior to the Act.

title: The Information Technology Act
shortDesc: The Information Technology Act, 2000 is India's primary cyber law. It gives legal recognition to electronic records, e-signatures, and e-governance, regulates Certifying Authorities and intermediaries, and defines cyber offences and their penalties.

rules: ITA-06 (Intermediary): Observe the due diligence required of an intermediary. Breach: Failure to observe the prescribed due diligence. Penalty: Loss of the safe-harbour exemption u/s 79(1), so the intermediary becomes liable for the third-party information; failure to preserve required information -> s.67C (up to 3 years and fine).

ITA-07 (CyberCafe): Register, identify users and maintain logs as an intermediary (cyber cafe). Breach: Failure to observe cyber-cafe due diligence (registration, user identification, logs). Penalty: Loss of the safe-harbour exemption u/s 79(1); residual contravention -> s.45.

ITA-08 (ServiceProvider): Report cyber incidents and comply with CERT-In directions. Breach: Failure to report a cyber incident or to comply with a CERT-In direction. penalties.text: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.

penalties.text: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine up to Rs.1 lakh, or both.

penalties.breach: Failure to assist interception/monitoring/decryption, or to comply with a blocking direction (Sections 69, 69A)
penalties.text: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.

penalties.breach: Failure to assist traffic-data monitoring for cyber security (Section 69B)
penalties.text: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.

penalties.breach: Securing unauthorised access to a Protected System (Section 70(3))
penalties.text: Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine.

penalties.breach: Failure to provide information to, or comply with directions of, CERT-In (Section 70B(7))
penalties.text: Imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine up to Rs.1 lakh, or both.

penalties.breach: Misrepresentation (Section 71), breach of confidentiality/privacy (Section 72), disclosure in breach of lawful contract (Section 72A), false electronic signature Certificate (Sections 73-74)
penalties.text: Sections 71/72: up to 2 years or fine up to Rs.1 lakh, or both. Section 72A: up to 3 years or fine up to Rs.5 lakh, or both. Sections 73/74: up to 2 years or fine up to Rs.1 lakh, or both.

penalties.breach: Offences by companies (Section 85)
penalties.text: The person in charge and responsible, and the company, are liable; officers liable where consent/connivance/neglect is proved.
